title: Inner-anodyne relative inclusion of the arrow-prism collage
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, internal functor simplicial sets, nerves and degreewise products from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], relative joins from [def-coef-infinity-relative-join], and inner anodyne maps from [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product]. Let $X$ be any small simplicial set, $B\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,X)$ any simplicial subset, and $v:B\to X$ target evaluation. Put $J=B\star_X X$ using $v$ and $1_X$. For an $n$-simplex $x$ of $J$, write $i\in\{-1,\ldots,n\}$ for its last initial-block index. Its data are an initial arrow prism $q:\Delta^1\times\Delta^i\to X$ and a target-coordinate simplex $\sigma:\Delta^n\to X$ with $q(1,-)=\sigma|_{[i]}$; when $i=-1$ there is no prism.
Let $P_x$ be the nerve of the poset with chains $s_0<\cdots<s_i$ and $t_0<\cdots<t_n$, and cross relations $s_j\leq t_l$ exactly for $j\leq l$, with no relation from a $t$ to an $s$. Let $Q_x\subseteq P_x$ be the union of the prism on $s_0,\ldots,s_i,t_0,\ldots,t_i$ and the simplex on all $t_l$. An empty source list is omitted. For a simplex operator $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, the maps $P_{\alpha^*x}\to P_x$ send each retained source or target vertex to the vertex of the same type with index $\alpha(j)$; these maps also take $Q_{\alpha^*x}$ into $Q_x$.
Define $P$ to be the degreewise quotient of $\coprod_{x\in J_n,\ n\geq0}P_x$ by all these simplex-operator identifications, with the induced simplicial operators, and let $Q\subseteq P$ be the union of the images of the $Q_x$. For any simplicial subset $H\subseteq J$, let $P_H\subseteq P$ be the union of the images of $P_h$ for all simplices $h$ of $H$. Then the inclusion $Q\cup P_H\hookrightarrow P$ is inner anodyne. Evaluation of the prism part by $q$ and of the target simplex by $\sigma$ gives a well-defined simplicial map $Q\to X$. The chains $s_0<\cdots<s_i<t_{i+1}<\cdots<t_n$ define a simplicial map $d:J\to P$, with the evident pure-factor conventions. No quasicategory hypothesis on $X$ is required.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, construction of S; the two-row support filtration from returned step 4, extracted as a relative inner-anodyne inclusion. Kerodon identifier, not a Stacks tag; read online. The explicit simplicial formulation is agent-written from the returned proof.

proof.text: Let $e:J\to\Delta^1$ record the join-block parameter of [def-coef-infinity-relative-join]. A simplex of $P_x$ is a weak chain $v_0\leq\cdots\leq v_m$. Record its indices $a:[m]\to[n]$ and its row $r:[m]\to[1]$ ($s$ has row $0$, $t$ row $1$). The cross relations say precisely that both maps are monotone and $e(x)a\leq r$. Assign this chain the pair $(r,a^*x)$. It respects every generating simplex-operator identification in the quotient. Conversely, a pair $(r,y)$ with $y\in J_m$ and $e(y)\leq r$ is represented in $P_y$ by the chain choosing $s_k$ when $r(k)=0$ and $t_k$ otherwise. Applying the support operator $a$ identifies this representative with the original chain in $P_x$. These two constructions are inverse in each degree and commute with precomposition. Hence, directly from the stated quotient, $P_m=\{(r,y):e(y)\leq r\}$ with coordinatewise simplicial operators. This is an explicit identification of this item's objects, not an assumption that the support maps $P_x\to P$ are injective.

source.place: Agent-written relative staircase expansion of the construction of S in Proposition 7.3.5.5; degreewise normal form for the quotient

proof.text: Write $J_0=e^{-1}(0)$ for the simplicial fiber, not the set of vertices. The full initial join factor identifies $J_0$ with $B$. In the normal form of step 1, the target simplex in each $Q_x$ gives exactly the pairs $(1,y)$. A chain in its prism has all indices in the initial block, and thus gives $e(y)=0$; conversely every pair with $e(y)=0$ is represented in the prism of $P_y$. Therefore $Q=(\{1\}\times J)\cup(\Delta^1\times J_0)$ inside $P$. Likewise $P_H=\{(r,y)\in P:y\in H\}$: one direction follows because $H$ is a simplicial subset; the other uses the representative in $P_y$. These formulas include degenerate supports and show that all these unions are simplicial subsets.

source.place: Agent-written relative staircase expansion of the construction of S in Proposition 7.3.5.5; identify the prescribed simplicial subset

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] to the second coordinate: write uniquely $y=a^*x$ for a surjective monotone $a:[m]\twoheadrightarrow[n]$ and nondegenerate $x\in J_n$. Since $a$ has a monotone section, $y\in H$ if and only if $x\in H$. For this fixed support, a pair $(r,a^*x)$ is degenerate in $P$ if and only if some adjacent positions have both the same $a$-value and the same $r$-value. In that case collapsing those positions produces its degeneracy explicitly. Conversely, if the pair is a degeneracy, its second coordinate and the uniqueness assertion force $a$ to factor through that degeneracy; its row factors too, giving such equal adjacent values. Thus every nondegenerate simplex of $P$ is represented by a strict chain in $P_x$ whose index map is surjective, with uniquely determined $x,a,r$. In particular two such representatives can coincide only when all three data coincide.

source.place: Agent-written relative staircase expansion of the construction of S in Proposition 7.3.5.5; unique nondegenerate support and the degeneracy test

proof.text:
For a support $x\in J_n$, let $i$ be its last initial-block index. If $i=-1$, only the target row is available, so all its chains lie in $Q$. If $i=n$, the whole $P_x$ is its prism, again in $Q$. If $x\in H$, all its chains lie in $P_H$. Otherwise $0\leq i<n$. A strict full-support chain outside $Q$ has a last source vertex $s_j$, $0\leq j\leq i$. All sources precede all targets. Surjectivity of its indices forces the sources to be exactly $s_0,\ldots,s_j$ and the targets to be $t_{j+1},\ldots,t_n$, with the sole optional additional vertex $t_j$. Thus the missing nondegenerate simplices, with this unique support, are exactly
$$A_{x,j}=(s_0,\ldots,s_j,t_{j+1},\ldots,t_n),\qquad B_{x,j}=(s_0,\ldots,s_j,t_j,t_{j+1},\ldots,t_n).$$
Their dimensions are $n$ and $n+1$. This exhausts the possibilities because any repeated index in a strict chain must occur at its single row change.

source.place: Agent-written relative staircase expansion of the construction of S in Proposition 7.3.5.5; enumerate the missing simplices; no separate comparison lemma is invoked

proof.text: Order attachments first by support dimension $n\geq1$, then by $j=0,\ldots,n-1$, using all eligible $x$ at a given $(n,j)$. For $B_{x,j}$, deleting $t_j$ gives $A_{x,j}$; the deleted vertex has position $j+1$, which is inner since $0<j+1<n+1$. Deleting $s_j$ gives $A_{x,j-1}$ for $j>0$, already attached, and gives the all-target simplex for $j=0$, in $Q$. Every other codimension-one face omits an index of $[n]$. Its second coordinate factors through a proper face of $x$, whose nondegenerate support has dimension at most $n-1$, so it is already present. The boundary of $A_{x,j}$ is present too: each of its faces omits an index. Consequently the prescribed part of the standard $(n+1)$-simplex $B_{x,j}$ is the horn $\Lambda^{n+1}_{j+1}$, and filling it adds precisely the two still-missing nondegenerate simplices $A_{x,j},B_{x,j}$.

source.place: Agent-written relative staircase expansion of the construction of S in Proposition 7.3.5.5; the inner horn and the complete face calculation

proof.text: Here the horn description is also valid globally, even when a support simplex has identified boundary faces. By the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] as applied in step 3, the two new simplices $A_{x,j},B_{x,j}$ are nondegenerate and do not identify with any simplex already present or with the two new simplices for another support. All their proper faces except $A_{x,j}$ are accounted for in step 5. Any identifications among those faces occur inside the already prescribed subset. Degeneracies introduce no further relations, since their unique nondegenerate representatives were determined in step 3. Thus maps defined on the old subset and on these standard simplices agree globally exactly when they agree on the displayed horns. This also proves independence of attachments for distinct $x$ at the same $(n,j)$. Starting with the entire $P_H$ changes nothing: a new simplex has support $x\notin H$, so it cannot lie in $P_H$, while faces whose supports lie in $H$ are already prescribed.

source.place: Agent-written relative staircase expansion of the construction of S in Proposition 7.3.5.5; compatibility under all quotient and degeneracy identifications, relative to arbitrary H

proof.text: Test the inclusion against any inner fibration $p:E\to F$ in the sense of [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product]. Given a commutative square with top $Q\cup P_H\to E$ and bottom $P\to F$, extend its top map in the order of step 5. At each $(n,j)$ and each eligible $x$, the old map supplies the horn $\Lambda^{n+1}_{j+1}\to E$, and the composite $\Delta^{n+1}\xrightarrow{B_{x,j}}P\to F$ supplies the bottom simplex. The right lifting property of $p$ gives a filler; give $A_{x,j}$ the missing face of that filler. Step 6 proves the choices agree on every overlap. Choose the fillers for each small family, continue through the finite list of $j$ for each $n$, and take the union over $n$. Every simplex is a degeneracy of one classified in step 4 or is initially prescribed, so the union is a simplicial lift on all of $P$. This proves the left lifting property against every inner fibration, precisely the definition of inner anodyne in the cited node. Neither a model-category theorem nor closure under transfinite compositions is being used without a citation.

source.place: Agent-written relative staircase expansion of the construction of S in Proposition 7.3.5.5; construct the relative lift directly from inner horn lifting

proof.text: It remains to construct the other asserted maps. By [def-coef-infinity-relative-join], $J_0=B$, with target coordinate $v$, and the map $p_X:J\to X$ is $y\mapsto\sigma_y$. On $\Delta^1\times J_0\subseteq Q$ use evaluation $(t,b)\mapsto b(t)$, the counit specified degreewise by the internal functor definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. On $\{1\}\times J$ use $p_X$. Their intersection is $\{1\}\times B$, where both formulas equal $v$; hence they glue degreewise to a simplicial map $Q\to X$. In each $Q_x$ its prism formula is $q$ and its target-simplex formula is $\sigma$, including their common face because $q(1,-)=\sigma|_{[i]}$. This proves exactly the stated evaluation, including compatibility under every simplex operator.

source.place: Agent-written relative staircase expansion of the construction of S in Proposition 7.3.5.5; evaluation on Q and agreement on its overlap

proof.text: Finally $d_m(y)=(e(y),y)$ lies in $P_m$ by step 1 and commutes with every simplicial operator since $e$ is simplicial. Its representative in $P_y$ selects $s_0,\ldots,s_i,t_{i+1},\ldots,t_n$, exactly the required chain. For $i=-1$ it is the pure target chain and for $i=n$ the pure source chain. All arguments used only simplicial identities, the cited unique nondegenerate decomposition, and inner-horn lifting for the arbitrary test fibration. No quasicategory property of $X$ has entered.

lean.statement: theorem arrowPrismCollageInnerAnodyne (X : SSet.{u}) (B : ((ihom Δ[1]).obj X).Subcomplex) (H : (relativeJoin (arrowPrismTarget X B) (𝟙 X)).Subcomplex) : SSet.innerAnodyneExtensions (arrowPrismQHToP X B (arrowPrismTarget X B) H) ∧ ∃ (ev : (arrowPrismQ X B (arrowPrismTarget X B) : SSet) ⟶ X) (d : relativeJoin (arrowPrismTarget X B) (𝟙 X) ⟶ arrowPrismP X B (arrowPrismTarget X B)), (∀ (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (z : (arrowPrismQ X B (arrowPrismTarget X B)).obj n), z.val.1 = SSet.stdSimplex.objEquiv.symm (SimplexCategory.const n.unop ⦋1⦌ 1) → ev.app n z = (relativeJoinProjection (arrowPrismTarget X B) (𝟙 X)).app n z.val.2) ∧ (∀ (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (z : (arrowPrismQ X B (arrowPrismTarget X B)).obj n) (b : B.obj n), z.val.2 = (relativeJoinInl (arrowPrismTarget X B) (𝟙 X)).app n b → ev.app n z = ((ihom.ev Δ[1]).app X).app n (z.val.1, B.ι.app n b)) ∧ (∀ (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (y : (relativeJoin (arrowPrismTarget X B) (𝟙 X)).obj n), (d.app n y).val = ((relativeJoinSnd (arrowPrismTarget X B) (𝟙 X) ≫ fst _ _).app n y, y))
